title: Tenant session budgeter and probabilistic soft-degrade playbook
creator: Asha Menon
summary: Design and implement a tenant-aware session budgeting system plus a probabilistic soft-degrade strategy to keep latency SLOs during downstream Redis/Kafka/DB pressure. The feature introduces per-tenant session budgets, admission controls that can probabilistically skip non-critical downstream reads, and a shadowing pipeline to auto-tune circuit thresholds before rollouts.
background: We repeatedly see tail-latency and outage windows when downstream stateful stores (Redis/KV, Kafka, SQL) are saturated by bursty workloads. Existing coarse-grained connection pooling and reactive circuit breakers can either be too aggressive (causing broad user impact) or too permissive (letting SLOs blow). This ticket aims to build an operator-friendly playbook + implementation to: 1) bound per-tenant resource use, 2) gracefully degrade non-critical work with probabilistic skipping, and 3) auto-tune thresholds using shadowed traffic and offline metrics so the platform remains within its latency and availability SLOs during incidents.
proposed_solution: 1) Per-tenant session budgets: allocate a token budget per active session that limits concurrent downstream connections/slots and KV read budget. Budgets are derived from tenant plan and historical QPS percentiles. 2) Admission controller: envelopes requests through a lightweight local governor that either admits, queues (short bounded wait), or probabilistically soft-degrades non-essential reads (e.g., background feature cache refresh, non-canonical metadata). 3) Probabilistic soft-degrade logic: configurable skip rates per route and priority band with deterministic seeding for reproducibility. 4) Local stub cache + stale-while-revalidate: critical reads have a short stale fallback to avoid synchronously hitting backend under pressure. 5) Shadow tuning: run every request through a shadow path where alternative thresholds and circuit-breaker policies are simulated; offline jobs compute candidate thresholds to propose via rollout pipeline. 6) Multi-region failover: integrate budget cross-region awareness so that a regional overpressure triggers early routing to healthy regions based on SLO cost tradeoffs. 7) Circuit breakers auto-tuning: using shadow failure rates, latency distributions, and admission rejection signals to adjust tripping windows and half-open probe rates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) P99 tail latency for generation endpoints under 95th percentile burst test does not exceed baseline +10% in the canary region. 2) During induced Redis saturation test, at least 90% of high-priority requests are served from fresh data or short-stale fallback; overall error rate < 0.5%. 3) Automatic threshold proposals (from shadow tuning job) produce stable changes (no more than 3 successive rollbacks) during a 2-week pilot. 4) Playbook runbook validated with on-call and SRE sign-off and an incident play executed successfully in staging.
tasks: Write design doc: rationale, budgeting algorithm, failure modes (link below)
Implement local tenant budgeter middleware and per-route configuration hooks
Add probabilistic soft-degrade primitives to runtime (configurable skip rates and deterministic sampling)
Implement local stub/stale cache for critical read paths
Build shadow pipeline + offline tuning job (k8s Cron + metrics aggregator)
Integrate with multi-region router to surface budget saturation and trigger reroute heuristics
Add circuit breaker auto-tuning worker and expose proposals in Console
Create chaos+bench tests for Redis/Kafka/DB saturation scenarios
Documentation & runbook: on-call steps, rollback, escalation flow
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for budgeter logic and deterministic sampling. 2) Integration test: local dev harness with a Redis emulator to assert token accounting and probabilistic skips at known rates. 3) Staging chaos tests: use load generator to simulate tenant burst and downstream saturation; measure SLOs and verify soft-degrade preserves high-priority success. 4) Multi-region failover DR test: simulate regional KV outage and verify reroute / budget adoption in secondary region. 5) Shadow autonomy verification: ensure shadow jobs propose thresholds and that these proposals are reproducible from collected metrics.
monitoring_metrics:
- Per-tenant admission rate, queue time, token consumption
- Probabilistic-skip count per route and effective error delta
- P50/P95/P99 latency for priority bands
- Downstream error rates (429/503/timeout) and correlation with admission decisions
- Shadow-simulated break count and proposed threshold history
- Cross-region reroute counts and added tail latency
runbook_steps: 1) Detect: console alert when per-region downstream saturations hit >80% of connection budget for 3m. 2) Triage: check tenant-wide admission rejections and skip-rate. 3) Immediate mitigation: raise soft-degrade skip rate for non-critical routes by +X (auto-suggested value from shadow proposals). 4) If still failing, enable region-wide conservative reroute policy to healthy region for affected tenant segments. 5) Recovery: lower skip rates gradually and monitor shadow proposals to validate new thresholds. 6) Post-incident: capture metrics, run offline tuning and propose new default budgets for affected tenant class.
risk_and_mitigations:
Risk: Over-aggressive skipping may degrade user-visible quality. Mitigation: default high-priority read paths are excluded; sample-based quality checks during rollout.
Risk: Incorrect budget calculation penalizes small tenants. Mitigation: floor budgets and bootstrap grace windows.
Risk: Shadow pipeline introduces metric noise. Mitigation: deterministic sampling + sliding window smoothing and human review for proposals.
